back: The ordinary life of ordinary men wherein no one knows what thought they will next have, yet the collective life of humanity proceeds as though thoroughly scripted.
The certain man's method of turning his attention from his inner voices to those of others outside of him.
A discontent with no name, known to all men by its relentless flow and presence.
Either do something about what bothers you, or stop thinking about doing something.
Thinking of action comes into play when action seems impossible — which is why thinking of action won't get you anywhere.
For the rebel, acting and thinking-about-acting are two distinct things; his goal is to merge them.
Metaphorical locations in man's nervous system wherein AMv12 is depleted: by bodily health, by ordinary emotions, and by excitement of ordinary knowledge.
The natural inner movement toward an institutionalized existence; the final acceptance of civilized life and city thinking.
When you see clearly the reality of The Act and the helplessness of ordinary people; then you become responsible for your interactions with them.
Life has its own agenda and will not change it for you; the nervous-system-rebel holds a personal agenda beyond circumstances, accidents, or whims.
The intentional use of inner chemistry which a man with The Aim turns on his own automatic-consciousness as an affront to complacency and comfort.
To make consciousness conscious of itself and its heritage.
To bring consciousness under its control; to entertain only thoughts original with your consciousness; to develop a non-ordinary intention for your inner life.
Things men either don't understand or can't face.

front: ALL IS WRONG/ALL IS NOT RIGHT
back: Ordinary men's all-or-nothing is a cheap imitation of the rebel's do-or-die; in second reality everything is compromise.
An allegorical substance in the blood symbolizing the enriched fuel needed to push consciousness above its normal level.

front: ANYTHING YOU DON'T LIKE YOU WON'T BELIEVE
back: Anyone you don't like — you won't believe; no one can believe their self, the only source of the information needed to understand what's really going on.
The glasses through which ordinary consciousness views life; the rebel whispers 'apparently' before everything his ordinary mind says.
In the nervous-system-rebel an arranged marriage is between one's Aim and one's self; he marries his self and becomes one.
Not realizing the distinction between the physical and the intangible worlds; the failure to realize the reality of what you are.
The certain man's thinking as direct reception of information: no distortion, no filters — what goes in is what consciousness receives.
Man as the speaker to Life's amp; 95% of an amplifier's energy is wasted heat — should this sound familiar in a human context?
Consciousness in a state temperamentally unnatural for you.
The impression natural to automatic-consciousness that things are going to hell; an indirect manifestation of Life's own sensation of never accomplishing enough.
Reliance on something for which you have no proof; if you believe, you also not-believe — that does not equal real intelligence or thought.
Everything falls within the bell curve; as Life grows it pulls its extremes into the heart of the curve — same deal in your consciousness.
The functional range of ordinary consciousness: it allows thought to see only two sides to any issue, two aspects of Life itself.

Symbolic of men's emotional activity, between the Red (body) and Yellow (intellect); source of all religious, romantic, and poetic literature — and of emotions unprofitable to the man trying to get to the bottom of things.
Those who cannot act to satisfy themselves, and whose thinking-of-action is likewise unsatisfying. (The artists of the world.)
Everyone in the city feels broke because they have no one — no one IN them; the man who understands what's going on does, and thus can afford anything.
The rebel's attitude toward his self is 'It's all business' — treating his mentally conceived self as merchandise and his thoughts as fungible goods.
This one word describes the entire process of city life; the primo expression of binary consciousness, letting routine minds instantly switch sides in any conflict.
In man's intangible reality, by-products are often the product.
Humanity is in captivity — not exile; until you understand that, nothing will ever make sense save fairy tales and myths.
C Force is constructive energy; D Force destructive (or defender of the status quo); E Force everything else human-driven.
The nervous-system-rebel sees all men as dutiful cells working in the best interest of the larger cellular being, Life.
Everything in Life occurs at the cellular level; every action in the City is driven by cellular directives, though men believe otherwise.
'I'm hungry' — 'I'm horny' — 'Get out of my way'; the man getting to the bottom of things establishes a fourth one for his own private use.
Growth that is yet to be.
Change is the oxygen of Life's blood, yet the bane of its primary organ: human consciousness.
The opposite of anything bears the characteristics-cum-flaws of the original in reverse; any part of you that resists change will never understand it.
The rule of random certainty.
The certain man's Aim is to have no characteristics; to be a house with no furniture — no architectural style.
Life holds all the pieces; men are pawns moving only forward toward Life's aim of constant expansion; the certain man has removed his consciousness from the board.
The continual movement between the Three Forces; picture C, D & E as notes, and Life as a song in which they play off one another.
Life churns everyone's account for its profit, so all energies are traded and transformed; only the moment is of consequence to the man with The Aim.
Analogous to the body, the emotions, and the intellect. (Also: motion, heat & light.)
Use the fire in the belly to fuel the ice water in the brain — the furnace in the basement supplying heat for the penthouse.
Where no one is upset that the pail they are given is never filled; where people will do anything except what works.
The only suitable punctuation for a dedicated investigator; everything he thinks must be left open to further consideration.
In the City, all behavior is impulsive.
All growth is the complex consuming the simple; when your personal life ceases to be ever more complex — you're dying.
The willful behavior of a man with that special aim: doing and saying that which you are not by temperament inclined to do.
Theories of mortal conspiracies reflect ordinary consciousness' secular attempt to tie everything together.
Over a lifetime: the certain man's mental condition.
There is no connection between cost and need for the rebel; anything he can afford, he knows is no value to his struggle.
Life holds everyone's dance card, but the nervous-system-rebel harbors one of his own: 'I will not intangibly do what is natural to me.'
The totally uncontrolled flow of apparently random thoughts — enjoyed by all men, but never actually random: men only daydream of matters they have feelings about.
Life will allow you to do almost anything except get out of debt; Life will permit you to think almost anything — except that you are not in debt.
To see Life not as a blind machine but as a delightful, infinitely full living structure the Few can study and enjoy.
The '+' sign in the Equation 'I + Not-I = Everything'; the internal workings of Life's body; everyone else's genes.
The relationship between one person and the rest of life; the signs are verbs, and I and Everything are forever in flux.
Everything is everything else.
Even the most tyrannical rulers have a Freedom Day when people celebrate their good fortune at being tyrannized by such a wonderful despot.
What holds you together; the inner magnetic pull stabilizing your consciousness enough to give you a sense of a personal self.
Everything is due to heredity, and environment is the sum total of everyone else's heredity.
Anyone you gossip about.
The history of you divided into three eras: the barbarian, the troubadour, and the philosopher (Red, Blue & Yellow Circuits).
Health, wealth, worry.
With developed hearing you can listen to one thing but hear something else — necessary for getting to the bottom of things.
The ceaseless flow of Life; Life speaking for itself — through man; an endless verb which consciousness chops into digestible nouns.

front: INFORMATION & Its Necessary Movement For Profit
back: To make a profit, goods must be moved from production to where they are not produced — this applies to ideas; the rebel must move ideas internally to fresh markets.
Ordinary consciousness considers these two entirely different matters — which helps keep it ordinary.
The activation of one's intangible possibilities; by it one swallows the plus sign in 'I + Not-I = Everything', then consumes the Not-I.
Three intersecting circuits whereby Life's energy is converted into useable form within man's nervous system.
The way to increase your understanding of something is to go play in the irrelevant.

front: JUST PAST EVERYTHING IS ITSELF AGAIN
back: No matter how far change goes, you end up no more than a thought's breadth from where you started.
Ask of any duality: 'To What End does Life have things thus arranged? What profitable purpose is being served?'
In part, language is used to assign blame; if the city had a motto it could be 'Somebody's To Blame'.
Look away — always looking up just over the heads of thoughts, over all words and images, beyond to the infinite horizon.
If you want to know what is going on with Life — look.
Stay on it.
A part of the certain man's nervous system not permanently soldered into his persona — energy potential not yet channeled; where Life attempts to expand through your consciousness.
Any comment on what has happened to you.
The Straight Line Phenomenon: it can't happen — that's why it's magic.
Two dimensional descriptions of a three-dimensional reality; temporary, ever-changing, ultimately disposable.
To hit anything you must aim at it; the certain man has but one target: The Aim.
Behind the constant verbal 'I' lurk two me's: a real me and a sham me; the investigator operates not as a speaking 'I' but as a non-speaking Me.
That which is mechanical is that which is ordinary; under normal conditions man does nothing — everything is done through him, a cog in a living machine.
Cure by inquiry — the looking-into something broken fixes it; a man's internal problems cannot withstand clinical examination.

front: MINISTRIES OF DEPRESSION AND OF STIMULATION
back: Everyone's internal government includes these two ministries whose actions provide the emotional range for routine stability.
For the many: what they don't understand; for the few: what they do. Things that occur in the E Flow.
Supreme teaching aids; in man's inner world nothing can be directly taught — the certain man's education demands views transcending all impotent reasoning.
Yellow Circuit's attempt to utilize Red Circuit's non-verbal, cellular memory.
Thinking about something in a manner other than your native consciousness normally would — floating a thought above the grasp of either-true-or-false.
For information to be New it must be threatening to that which currently exists; it does not lend itself to debate or amendment.
All regular news is bad news; all good news is yet to be. The certain man's job is to continually produce his own good news.
What happens to you intangibly is of no significance until the cellular voices report on the matter.
To the person pursuing The Aim, nouns do not meaningfully exist: everything significant is a verb; Life itself is a process — not a thing.
A Subjective Man wants to see what he wants to see, while an Objective Man wants to see what is to be seen.
That which the ordinary see but never see the significance of — because it's obvious.
Sensible shoes for normal adults.
A cover up for lack of thought.
The certain man is a living palindrome: he reads the same forwards and backwards.
As imagined by ordinary minds: a place free of all change.
The man seeking the bottom of things uses parallax to alter his perception: if something bugs you — move — shift your inner position.
Things are not as they are — things are as they partially are; X partially seen is not seen as X, but as Y.
One image of Life on earth, with men the primary guests — but they are not simply at the party, they are inseparable from it.
The father of all names; the mother of all fears; that which by definition doesn't exist; the only place a man can sleep and dream.
There is some nourishment in everything: always a payoff to any energy exchange between two discrete entities.
Consciousness labels anything not fitting its model as imaginary — yet the imaginary influences the real; in man's intangible reality everything is the placebo effect.

front: PLURALITY OF THOUGHT & THE ILLUSION THEREOF
back: At the ordinary level there is no plurality of thought — only the appearance; only the man working for The Aim experiences true plurality, preparation for original thought.
People with no other talent — people with one talent: the ability to dominate.
All populaces are inescapably stupid; the mob comprising your automatic-consciousness is irredeemably dumb and cruel.
Real power does not discuss itself; it does not debate — it decrees — it exercises.
Power is invisible cause; control (apparent power) is visible effect; those who appear in control may not hold the power.
Must accept other men's definitions of reality; must believe in freedom of will and fear change; are in charge of protecting the status quo.
The difference between them is that one involves spectators.
The undifferentiated energy of Life; everything the Yellow Circuit has named is the Primal Flow divided and given form, surging through Red, Blue, then Yellow circuits.
Silent information; the only information useful to the explorer, because it is original to him and only he knows it. It cannot be told.
If they're not chemical they're not real problems; the certain man sees that what others call problems is in truth the people themselves.
In the city, the illusion that you can get more out of a system than you put into it.
From the rebel's view all non-physical ills are psychosomatic; if it's making you sick and you can't touch it, you suffer from normal human consciousness.
The purpose of a thing cannot be stated; nothing works to its stated purpose; everything works to work.
Be out to solve it.

front: The QUESTION (One Of A Dozen Versions Of The Supreme Muser)
back: Am I conscious, or — is consciousness me?
A buffering of yourself from the fact that you don't know what's going on.
Real actions are not dependent on reasons: only impotent actions require reasoning.
Information that stimulates extraordinary growth in your nervous system.
You're not really rich until you don't care; not rich in knowledge until it means nothing to you; not rich in spirit until you don't care how you feel about how you feel.
One who can keep a diary and never use the word 'I'.
One whose being has as much beneficial effect on his patients as do his prescriptions.
Knows everything ordinary men believe about intangible matters is not — and neither is its opposite; indifferent foremost to his self.
A tight ship with a loose cargo: appearing a well-held-together noun, but in truth an internal verb loose as a goose.
Reasons exist only in the city; looking for reasons with a binary mind in a three-dimensional reality is folly.
The substitution of one habit for another.
Friendly kings lead their countries into war for mutual benefit; picture C & D Forces as the two kings — what might you learn about your own Yellow Circuit?
Where there is always another relevant observation to be made after one's original insight.
An invisible process whereby those who know of it bolster their metaphorical blood by not squandering AMv12; you cannot inherit it — only you can cause it in yourself.
The notion that there is such is one of Life's greatest diversionary ploys.
Each person's premier thespian effort; the rebel's sincerity is willful — he hugs Life and says 'I love you guy' — then forgets about it.
The only real solution is one that renders a problem irrelevant.
There is an unknown Song of Life — rhythm, melody, words; each circuit plays its part, and the Few bathe in its glory.
There is no such thing.
The certain man's willfully staged set-to between staring and not staring: the eyeball announcement of one's state of consciousness.
Man's inner state is a cell in Life with porous walls; only the new consciousness born of exploration has actual borders.

front: The STOP AND TAKE A LOOK METHOD
back: Constantly stop and grab the last thought that passed through your mind and take a look at it — then let it go and grab the next.
Nothing goes therein.
The routine mind's concept of cause & effect; the underlying reality is omni-direction movement — everything affects everything but does not cause it.
A personal form of hostility and expression of stupidity: announcing 'Things should not be as they are' — a denunciation of Life.
The art of being able to minimize fear, hesitation, and stagnation.
Survival with the addition of the loss of stupid certainty.
A unique non-physical symbiosis between humans transferring verbal energy to keep man's belief systems alive: 'Keep talking Horatio, or the boat will surely sink.'
Everything is symptom; there is no base illness behind the symptoms men perceive; the symptoms are it — the beginning and end.
Lack of talent manifests as desire for dominance; everyone's neural kingdom is born ruled by one with no talent but the urge to dominate.
Real talent is a personal activity that provides C Force based pleasure and requires no audience.
It's all just sound waves; some are rock & roll, some baroque chamber, others country & western — but it's still all just sound waves.
That which helps ordinary people remain sane and ordinary; the purpose of routine talk is to adjust one's self to the inevitable.
Dividing reality anew so that a few might glimpse the original unity.
Paper is alive — it talks and alters the molecular structure of one's nervous system; nothing man has made part of his life is not alive.
Primary source of undiagnosed conspiracies; the unseen voice of man's collective consciousness.
The Yellow Circuit's version of action — or its substitution for action.
The puzzle-solver's method for sticky choices: willful abandonment of anything ordinary men label a problem.
Living under threat produces heightened physical efficiency; the certain man's self-generated threat is all benefit.
Men live in tri-layered time: the bottom layer (Red Circuit) the past, the middle (Blue) the present, the upper (Yellow) the future.
Past, present, future reflect the Three Forces (D, E, C) and the Three Circuits (Red, Blue, Yellow); to awake is to be free of time zones.
What every human system suffers; known in the city as problems, primarily emotional botherations.
Ordinary consciousness sees only two legs to every stool whereas three are always present; no stool stands on two legs.
One who perceives from an extraordinary perspective in 3 ways, such that no looseness of possibility remains.
Ideas that are debatable and amendable (as opposed to correct & useful).
If you can perceive it — it's true; if Life dropped the Not-True, man would have only two dimensions.
Man's truth is perishable, and does not travel well, neither in time nor spatially.
The noise people make; what a person already agrees with; what maintains the Yellow Circuit's status quo.
One: when this Universe began; two: when the Yellow Circuit appeared in man's brain and consciousness commenced.
A good city tyrant makes people believe he knows everything they say and think; a would-be rebel counters by never denying any accusation.
Take yourself out of the mental picture, then look at everyone else.

front: UNDERSTANDING (Compared To What The Ordinary Call Knowledge)
back: Understanding is original knowledge, alive in the moment and in you; knowledge merely makes you comfortable in the city.
As opposed to Local View, it runs at right angles to men's routine 3-D perception: your view is Universal when you can look without you being at the heart of the looking.
The facility whereby a man can look at his self and miss the point.
It is the nature of being alive; Life is continually off balance; certain things can only be accomplished when off balance.
Upper hungers are unsatisfiable, non-edible versions of lower desires; lower hungers are necessity, upper ones are status.
Yellow Circuit ideas obtained from another person, as opposed to fresh food produced by your own investigations.
That which is original with you.
Words have the capacity to apparently wrap things up so matters seem concluded; but things do not come to an end — they recycle ad infinitum.
In each person a public voice and a private voice (plus the unspeaking Primal Force voice); all conflicts unique to humans are based on two Voices.
The voice of events-out-there speaks to no one personally; it is your cellular voice editorializing to consciousness that makes life irksome.
Existing on externally acquired information.
The only force in the Universe with the potential to overwhelm reality; chew toys for the mind; Yellow Circuit's blood.
There is no truth in words — yet coevally all truth in words; sound is linear and reality is not.

front: The WORLD IS BIG ENOUGH FOR EVERYBODY
back: If they weren't meant to be here, they wouldn't be; the inner outlier understands there is no one to criticize.
Happiness sans self interest; a feeling about Life not tied to your feelings about yourself.

back: Appear to be involved in some deliberate activity, or else totally at ease.

front: Code of Conduct #088 — complete the maxim (what does #088 say?)
back: Refrain from putting your name on possessions.

front: Code of Conduct #089 — complete the maxim (what does #089 say?)
back: Always wear your armor, and under it, your camouflage garb.

front: Code of Conduct #090 — complete the maxim (what does #090 say?)
back: Act as though you don't know the word envy.

front: Code of Conduct #091 — complete the maxim (what does #091 say?)
back: Accept no credit, and arrest any desire to seek it.

front: Code of Conduct #092 — complete the maxim (what does #092 say?)
back: Avoid publicity.

front: Code of Conduct #093 — complete the maxim (what does #093 say?)
back: You can appear ordinary, but not common.

front: Code of Conduct #094 — complete the maxim (what does #094 say?)
back: There is no need to be uncomfortable.

front: Code of Conduct #095 — complete the maxim (what does #095 say?)
back: Shed the appearance of being a consumer of any sort.

front: Code of Conduct #096 — complete the maxim (what does #096 say?)
back: Forsake comment on the failures of any Institutions.

front: Code of Conduct #097 — complete the maxim (what does #097 say?)
back: Keep no photographs of yourself.

front: Code of Conduct #098 — complete the maxim (what does #098 say?)
back: If you must deal with relatives treat them like foreign dignitaries.

front: Code of Conduct #099 — complete the maxim (what does #099 say?)
back: Steer clear of solemn talk with solemn people.

front: Code of Conduct #100 — complete the maxim (what does #100 say?)
back: Adopt a Personal Code of Quietness.

front: Code of Conduct #101 — complete the maxim (what does #101 say?)
back: Decline to comment on, or compliment people's possessions.

front: Code of Conduct #102 — complete the maxim (what does #102 say?)
back: Eschew verbal, fad words and phrases. Drive slow.

front: Code of Conduct #103 — complete the maxim (what does #103 say?)
back: Act completely confident under all circumstances; never let them see you confused, or hesitant.

front: Code of Conduct #104 — complete the maxim (what does #104 say?)
back: Forbear to correct people.

front: Code of Conduct #105 — complete the maxim (what does #105 say?)
back: If you suspect you might have to subsequently apologize for some particular behavior, don't behave.

front: Code of Conduct #106 — complete the maxim (what does #106 say?)
back: If possible, do not wear a watch.

front: Code of Conduct #107 — complete the maxim (what does #107 say?)
back: Never appear hungry.

front: Code of Conduct #108 — complete the maxim (what does #108 say?)
back: Speak moderately, and never raise your voice, or shout.

front: Code of Conduct #109 — complete the maxim (what does #109 say?)
back: Appear reasonably kind.

front: Code of Conduct #110 — complete the maxim (what does #110 say?)
back: Refuse to show your wounds, or point out your deformities.

front: Code of Conduct #111 — complete the maxim (what does #111 say?)
back: Withhold any acknowledgement of enemies.

front: Code of Conduct #112 — complete the maxim (what does #112 say?)
back: Dress with the latest fads only if you can pull it off correctly.

front: Code of Conduct #113 — complete the maxim (what does #113 say?)
back: Check any mention of your health.

front: Code of Conduct #114 — complete the maxim (what does #114 say?)
back: Although there is little really worth buying, there's no need to appear cheap.

front: Code of Conduct #115 — complete the maxim (what does #115 say?)
back: Try to interfere with people becoming impressed by you; at the very least, keep them from saying so.

front: Code of Conduct #116 — complete the maxim (what does #116 say?)
back: Reveal no information regarding your family, religion, education, or place of birth.

front: Code of Conduct #117 — complete the maxim (what does #117 say?)
back: Don't discuss yesterday.

front: Code of Conduct #118 — complete the maxim (what does #118 say?)
back: Be simple and direct.

front: Code of Conduct #119 — complete the maxim (what does #119 say?)
back: Squelch any desire to mention habits-abandoned, or sights-seen.

front: Code of Conduct #120 — complete the maxim (what does #120 say?)
back: Pick up after yourself, leave no visible trail.

front: Code of Conduct #121 — complete the maxim (what does #121 say?)
back: Try to avoid buying new stuff.

front: Code of Conduct #122 — complete the maxim (what does #122 say?)
back: Refer to your present abode as your house, never your home.

front: Code of Conduct #123 — complete the maxim (what does #123 say?)
back: Let no one hear you whine, or complain.

front: Code of Conduct #124 — complete the maxim (what does #124 say?)
back: Be judicious with any use of euphemisms, and do not speak in metaphors when you intend the literal.

front: Code of Conduct #125 — complete the maxim (what does #125 say?)
back: Never be cynical, sarcastic, or rude to anyone.

front: Code of Conduct #126 — complete the maxim (what does #126 say?)
back: Keep your distance from any group, organization, or institution.

front: Code of Conduct #127 — complete the maxim (what does #127 say?)
back: Move smoothly, or don't move at all.

front: Code of Conduct #128 — complete the maxim (what does #128 say?)
back: Remember, secrecy is good taste; that's all you need to know.

front: Code of Conduct #129 — complete the maxim (what does #129 say?)
back: Smile at everything.

front: Code of Conduct #130 — complete the maxim (what does #130 say?)
back: Act as though the world is big enough for everybody.

front: Code of Conduct #131 — complete the maxim (what does #131 say?)
back: Speak less than those with whom you're speaking.

front: Code of Conduct #132 — complete the maxim (what does #132 say?)
back: Anything you must be talked into, you shouldn't be.

front: Code of Conduct #133 — complete the maxim (what does #133 say?)
back: Keep quiet about age.

front: Code of Conduct #134 — complete the maxim (what does #134 say?)
back: Give no appearance of regret.

front: Code of Conduct #135 — complete the maxim (what does #135 say?)
back: Stay lean, and this, far beyond the physical.

front: Code of Conduct #136 — complete the maxim (what does #136 say?)
back: Be exact: say “I will not,” not, “I cannot.”

front: Code of Conduct #137 — complete the maxim (what does #137 say?)
back: Remember, to others, appearances are damn near everything.

front: Code of Conduct #138 — complete the maxim (what does #138 say?)
back: Be prepared for death; not merely the physical, but the annihilation of your status preference.

front: Code of Conduct #139 — complete the maxim (what does #139 say?)
back: All things, great and small come to an end; act as though you think of this constantly.

front: Code of Conduct #140 — complete the maxim (what does #140 say?)
back: Befriend no one who has not respect. Walk in no one's shadow.

front: Code of Conduct #141 — complete the maxim (what does #141 say?)
back: Withhold your praise from the weak and unjust.

front: Code of Conduct #142 — complete the maxim (what does #142 say?)
back: In worldly matters, always say what you're going to say before you have to actually say it.

front: Code of Conduct #143 — complete the maxim (what does #143 say?)
back: Every moment, and every movement should be in service to the Revolution. Ask your adversaries to continually restate their position.

front: Code of Conduct #144 — complete the maxim (what does #144 say?)
back: You may appear to go along, but you cannot fit.

front: Code of Conduct #145 — complete the maxim (what does #145 say?)
back: If you must apologize for someone, do it only once.

front: Code of Conduct #146 — complete the maxim (what does #146 say?)
back: Cultivate courage, not strategy; actual combat requires execution, not artful maneuvers. Even if you're lame, don't limp where it counts.

front: Code of Conduct #147 — complete the maxim (what does #147 say?)
back: Strive daily for a better understanding of the Revolution, and your duty; do not believe that you have achieved it today.

front: Code of Conduct #148 — complete the maxim (what does #148 say?)
back: Remain open twenty-four hours a day, and adopt an equal access policy for all new ideas, and customers.

front: Code of Conduct #149 — complete the maxim (what does #149 say?)
back: See clearly the distinction between interest and expected success.

front: Code of Conduct #150 — complete the maxim (what does #150 say?)
back: Conduct yourself as though you were the first to discover that no one's perfect.

front: Code of Conduct #151 — complete the maxim (what does #151 say?)
back: Set your behavior, and other Revolutionary matters, free from the calculations of potential profit-&-loss.

front: Code of Conduct #152 — complete the maxim (what does #152 say?)
back: Show no interest in “fake,” that is, City-notions of elegance.

front: Code of Conduct #153 — complete the maxim (what does #153 say?)
back: While still being civil and courteous, remember that it is City dwellers who are bothered with “status” and the “impression they make”; the Revolutionist cannot be concerned with what others may think of him.

front: Code of Conduct #154 — complete the maxim (what does #154 say?)
back: Cultivate the fear of but one thing, the disgrace in failure-of-duty (to your Aim).

front: Code of Conduct #155 — complete the maxim (what does #155 say?)
back: Save your love for the living, and your respect for the duty bound.

front: Code of Conduct #156 — complete the maxim (what does #156 say?)
back: Thou shalt not whine.

front: Code of Conduct #157 — complete the maxim (what does #157 say?)
back: Don't speak of things as being “unlikely,” or “improbable,” just say, “It's possible.”
